mission.display_title: Test acceptability of a fitted GLM
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to use Pearson's chi-square test and the likelihood-ratio test to judge acceptability of a fitted GLM — so tests are named and purposeful.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force naming both tests and when each is used — refuse p-value theatre without hypothesis.
mission.learning_objective: Apply statistical tests to determine the acceptability of a fitted model: Pearson's chi-square test and the likelihood-ratio test.
mission.concept_focus: Fitted GLM → Pearson χ² acceptability test → likelihood-ratio test.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday residual types (4.2.8). Today formal tests.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to apply Pearson's χ² and likelihood-ratio tests to judge acceptability of a fitted GLM.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name Pearson χ² and likelihood-ratio tests in GLM context.
State what 'acceptability' means for a fitted model at a high level.
Refuse reporting a p-value without stating the comparison.
task_descriptions: Sketch two test names before CMP.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.9
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name the two tests in 4.2.9. In one sentence each, what question does each help answer about a fitted GLM?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Pearson χ²: assess fit/acceptability of fitted model. LRT: compare models / nested hypotheses about parameters (as CMP frames).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.9
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You have a fitted GLM and want to judge acceptability. (1) State what Pearson's χ² test and the likelihood-ratio test each compare (in outline), and what you must state before quoting a p-value. (2) Refuse: 'Interpreting every coefficient in the software output finishes applying acceptability tests.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Pearson χ²: aggregate squared Pearson residuals against a χ² reference (adequacy of fit). LRT: compares likelihood/deviance of the fitted model to a relevant nested or saturated alternative. Before quoting a p-value, state the hypotheses / what is being compared and the reference distribution. (2) Refuse: coefficient interpretation is a different LO; today requires applying the formal acceptability tests.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Quoting p-values without stating the comparison, or substituting coefficient tourism for GOF tests.
